classification.habit: Woody climbing shrub or twining climber
classification.habitat: Dry and moist deciduous forest margins, scrub and cultivated areas
classification.distribution: Tropical and subtropical regions of the Indian subcontinent

identification.description: A woody climber with opposite leaves and small greenish-yellow flowers; the leaves are the characteristic medicinal part.
identification.whole_plant: Perennial woody climber/twiner, often scrambling through surrounding vegetation.
identification.root: Slender to moderately stout root; medicinal identity should be confirmed from authenticated material.
identification.stem: Woody, branched, cylindrical to slightly angular young branches.
identification.leaf: Opposite, simple, elliptic to ovate leaves with entire to slightly wavy margins and a short petiole.
identification.flower: Small greenish to yellowish flowers borne in axillary clusters.
identification.fruit: Paired follicles, slender and elongated, developing after flowering.
identification.seed: Seeds are borne inside the follicles and may have a light tuft of hairs.
identification.bark: Thin bark on younger branches; older stems become more corky and woody.
identification_points: Authenticate the drug before medicinal use

therapeutics.precautions: Use authenticated material; clinical use should follow an appropriate Ayurvedic reference and practitioner guidance.

phytochemistry.chemical_notes: Gymnemic acids are characteristic constituents reported from the leaves; exact profile varies with material and extraction.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Gymnema sylvestre has been studied extensively for metabolic and glucose-related effects; this project does not infer clinical efficacy from preclinical or limited human evidence.
modern_information.safety_notes: Potential effects on glucose handling are relevant when combined with glucose-lowering therapy; clinical supervision is appropriate.

exam_points: Gymnemic acids are characteristic leaf constituents
viva_questions: What is the botanical name of Meshashrungi?
Which family does Meshashrungi belong to?

mnemonics: Gymnema = Gudmar/Meshashrungi; think metabolic-use study and opposite leaves.
student.quick_revision: Meshashrungi (Gymnema sylvestre): woody climber, Apocynaceae; leaf and root are used; gymnemic acids are characteristic constituents.

teaching_points: Demonstrate opposite leaves and twining habit.
Discuss botanical authentication and distinction from unrelated climbers.
discussion_points: Classical Prameha context versus modern metabolic research
practical_points: Observe leaf arrangement, venation and petiole.
Examine authenticated fruiting material when available.

doctor.quick_reference: Meshashrungi is traditionally used in Prameha-related contexts; identify the drug correctly and avoid substituting unverified climbers.
key_precautions: Consider glucose-lowering medicines and monitor clinically when relevant
Do not treat traditional indications as proof of modern efficacy
